title: Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Smashes $21M+ Preview, Lionsgate’s 2nd Best 2026 Box Office】
body:
The latest installment of the Hunger Games saga has surged ahead of expectations, racking up more than $21 million in advance ticket sales and positioning itself as the second‑largest preview haul of any film released in 2026. The figure also marks the second‑best opening for the franchise, underscoring Lionsgate’s ability to command the Thanksgiving weekend box office even without the usual tentpoles from Disney’s “Wicked” or “Moana” sequels.

The $21.25 million preview total was compiled from a combination of early‑bird tickets, premium‑format reservations and a robust digital marketing push that has tapped into both longtime fans and a new generation of viewers. Industry analysts note that the momentum is especially impressive given the crowded holiday calendar, which typically sees studios stacking high‑budget spectacles to capture family audiences. Lionsgate’s strategic timing—dropping the film on the Thursday before Thanksgiving—has allowed it to dominate the early‑week ticketing window, a period traditionally dominated by Disney and Warner Bros. releases.

Beyond the raw numbers, the film’s performance signals a broader shift in how franchise properties are being leveraged in the post‑pandemic market. The Hunger Games brand, which first captivated audiences a decade ago, has been carefully rejuvenated through a blend of fresh talent, contemporary storytelling, and a heightened emphasis on visual spectacle. The sequel, “Sunrise on the Reaping,” expands the dystopian world with new characters and a plot that intertwines political intrigue with personal survival, aiming to resonate with both nostalgic viewers and younger demographics drawn to socially relevant narratives. Early audience surveys suggest that the film’s thematic focus on collective resistance and environmental stewardship is striking a chord, potentially widening its appeal beyond the core fan base.

Lionsgate’s success also highlights the studio’s evolving distribution strategy. By prioritizing advanced ticket sales and premium‑format experiences—such as IMAX, Dolby Cinema, and 4DX—the company has extracted higher per‑ticket revenue while creating a sense of event viewing that encourages early commitment. Moreover, the studio has capitalized on data‑driven targeting, using social‑media analytics to pinpoint regions with historically strong franchise performance and tailoring localized promotional campaigns accordingly. This approach appears to have paid dividends, as several mid‑size markets reported preview sales that outpaced those of comparable blockbusters released earlier in the year.

The strong preview showing bodes well for the film’s opening weekend, which is projected to surpass $70 million domestically, potentially eclipsing the franchise’s previous best. If the momentum holds, “Sunrise on the Reaping” could become the highest‑grossing Hunger Games entry to date, reinforcing Lionsgate’s position as a formidable contender in the holiday box‑office race. The film’s performance may also influence studio decision‑making regarding future franchise expansions, with the possibility of green‑lighting additional sequels, spin‑offs, or even a streaming series that builds on the same universe.

Looking ahead, the industry will be watching how “Sunrise on the Reaping” fares against the inevitable competition from Disney’s late‑December releases and the spring slate of superhero outings. Regardless of the outcome, the film’s early success demonstrates that well‑managed legacy properties can still generate significant excitement and revenue in a market increasingly dominated by streaming and franchise fatigue. As Thanksgiving approaches, audiences can expect a crowded theater landscape, but Lionsgate’s latest offering appears poised to claim a prominent share of the holiday box‑office crown.
